note: Anchors are verbatim upstream substrings. `alt` gives the restated anchor used by a candidate when an edit changed the wording; a requirement is covered when every anchor (or its declared alternative) is present. Section checks (`sections`) require every line of that upstream section to appear verbatim.

requirements.statement: Discovery trigger: use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code.
anchors: description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code

requirements.statement: Always applies to new features, bug fixes, refactoring and behavior changes.
Exceptions (throwaway prototypes, generated code, configuration files) require asking the human partner.
Wanting to skip TDD 'just this once' is rationalization.
anchors: Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

requirements.statement: Prose for humans and trivial code earn no test (stated only in the resource).
resource_anchors: trivial code and human prose earn none

requirements.statement: If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know it tests the right thing.
anchors: **Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

requirements.statement: The letter of the rules is the spirit of the rules.
anchors: **Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

requirements.statement: Iron Law: no production code without a failing test first.
anchors: NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST

requirements.statement: Code written before its test is deleted and reimplemented from tests; not kept, adapted or consulted.
anchors: Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

requirements.statement: Cycle order: RED, Verify RED, GREEN, Verify GREEN, REFACTOR, then the next failing test.
RED: one minimal test of one behavior, clearly named, using real code (mocks only if unavoidable).
anchors: Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

requirements.statement: Test quality: one thing ('and' in name means split), name describes behavior, demonstrates desired API.
Read writing-good-tests.md when writing or changing any test (four listed rules).
anchors: When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md)
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

requirements.statement: Verify RED is mandatory: run the test; it fails (not errors), with the expected message, because the feature is missing.
Test passes at RED: it tests existing behavior; fix the test.
anchors: **Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

requirements.statement: Test errors at RED: fix the error and re-run until it fails correctly.
anchors: **Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

requirements.statement: Wrong failure at RED: go back to RED (stated only in the upstream diagram).

alt.verify_red -> red [label=\"wrong\\nfailu: **Fails for another reason?** Go back to RED and correct the test.

requirements.statement: GREEN: simplest code that passes; no features, other refactors or improvements beyond the test.
anchors: Write simplest code to pass the test.
Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

requirements.statement: Verify GREEN is mandatory: the test passes, other tests pass, output pristine.
Test fails at GREEN: fix the code, not the test.
Other tests fail at GREEN: fix now (see T4).
Run the project's full suite even when the task names one file; scope bounds the deliverable, not verification; report every failure by name, including ones you didn't cause.
anchors: **"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.**
A scope statement in your task bounds the
including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name

requirements.statement: REFACTOR only after green (duplication, names, helpers); keep tests green; add no behavior.
anchors: Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

requirements.statement: Repeat with the next failing test for the next feature.
anchors: Next failing test for next feature.

requirements.statement: Rationalization rebuttals (11 rows), kept verbatim.
Red flags (13) mean: delete code, start over with TDD.
sections: ## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

requirements.statement: Verification checklist (8 items) before marking work complete; any unchecked box means TDD was skipped: start over.
When stuck: don't know how to test means write the wished-for API, assertion first, ask your human partner; design rows.
Bug found: write a failing test reproducing it; never fix bugs without a test.
anchors: Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.
Never fix bugs without a test.

requirements.statement: Final Rule: production code means a test exists and failed first; no exceptions without your human partner's permission.
anchors: Production code → test exists and failed first
No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

requirements.statement: writing-good-tests.md present and byte-identical; it names superpowers:writing-skills (not packaged).
